data.narrative:
Epsilon3, a Series A-stage space and aerospace company founded by Laura Crabtree and Max Mednik, has raised $19M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a landscape of 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and Planet Labs, though narrow-filter peer matching proved insufficient for direct median-based anchoring.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable approach, using the company's $19M total raised as a proxy baseline and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to next-stage transitions. This yields an implied valuation of $38M. The public-comp anchoring method, while informative (Space & Aerospace median P/S of 27.4x across the six traded comps), cannot be operationalized absent Epsilon3's disclosed revenue. Peer-median triangulation was rejected due to insufficient same- or adjacent-stage private comparables meeting data density thresholds.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $32M to $44M, with a median of $38M. This range reflects primary reliance on stage-progression mechanics rather than market-comparable validation. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue disclosure (precluding multiples-based cross-check), limited availability of comparable Series A-stage private Space & Aerospace data, and the wide dispersion inherent in early-stage frontier-tech valuations. Additional financials would strengthen confidence in this estimate.
